experiment_template.research_question: Does removing the byte-preservation conflict improve genuine repairs?
stop_conditions: No field injection or serving activation.
No live dispatch before exact experiment binding.

success_criteria.controls: same pager, schema, contract, prompt load, provider settings and fixture; change only this system sentence
success_criteria.primary: fewer unchanged-source proposals without negative semantic comparison
success_criteria.status: candidate; exact sample and physical-call caps must be bound before execution

falsifier: Under a separately frozen paired live test, unchanged-source failures do not decrease or semantic correctness regresses; the wording alone is not established as causal by static inspection.
mechanism: Literal byte preservation in the higher-priority system message can dominate repair intent and a later user-level review card. The candidate removes this conflict without changing scope, schema or pager.
scope: Prospective candidate only, motivated during H14 by a verified unchanged-source proposal. No H15 live experiment has run; do not relabel H14 as a test of this instruction change.
statement: The system instruction to preserve every source byte conflicts with repairing code and contributes to unchanged-source proposals; distinguishing required edits from unrelated behavior will reduce that failure.
